reasoning_traces.think:
The receiver separation tendency is derived through empirical Bayes shrinkage of raw separation distances observed in 1,960 (game, play, receiver) triplets. This process involves combining pooled and family-based features into a composite vector, joining with receiver identifiers, deduplicating, and mapping NFL IDs to GSIS IDs. The resulting shrunk estimates reflect posterior means under a normal prior, with weights indicating confidence. The tendency is structurally aligned with a ShrunkEstimate interface that supports both raw and adjusted values. However, the calibrated regime cannot proceed due to insufficient truth set coverage—only 67 frames exist across three plays in the canonical validation sample. This limitation implies that while the tendency is usable in an uncalibrated mode, it cannot yet support precise per-play modeling without further data integration. The failure mode lies in the lack of synchronized tracking and event labeling, which blocks the application of standard calibration techniques such as Platt scaling or isotonic regression.
